title: Tagged I/O tiered pricing + streaming floor experiment for Hosted API and contract alignment
creator: Maya Singh
description: We will run a multi-armed experiment to evaluate a tagged I/O pricing model for the Hosted API that separates input and output token rates with explicit streaming discounts and a configurable enterprise 'billing floor' tied to contract SKUs. This ticket covers experiment design, instrumenting tagged usage buckets, contract language proposals, legal/security questionnaire alignment, and rollout gating criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment exposes distinct cohorts with: (a) symmetric IO pricing baseline, (b) asymmetric IO pricing (cheaper input tokens), (c) asymmetric IO + streaming discount, (d) enterprise floor variant; all cohorts tracked for 8 weeks
Billing reports show per-customer reconciliation within 0.5% of true usage across tagged buckets
No more than 5% of customers in test cohorts file billing disputes attributable to tagging errors
Sales + Legal sign off on proposed contract wording and security questionnaire addendum
Decision made to roll one variant to GA or iterate based on pre-defined metric thresholds
experiment_plan: Design: create four pricing arms (Baseline, IO-split, IO-split+streaming, IO-split+streaming+contract-floor). Randomize new signups and a subset of existing low-risk accounts. Instrument: add 'io_tag' metadata to per-request records, extend billing pipeline to compute separate ingress/egress sub-meters, implement streaming-duration discount applied at token-level for streamed responses. Contract floor: add a toggle that enforces a monthly minimum invoice if enterprise SKU enabled; billing UI shows projected floor impact. Timeline: 8-week test window with 2-week warm-up. Rollout gates: data completeness, absence of systemic billing regressions, legal/finance approval. Communication: update pricing docs, add FAQ for customers in test cohorts.
decisions: Prefer asymmetric pricing if ARPC increases >3% without >2% increase in disputes
Only enable contract-floor for customers with Sales-verified consent and explicit SKU mapping
Streaming discount capped at 20% to avoid long-tail cost exposure
risks: Metering mismatches from proxy caching leading to misattributed input tokens
Customers seeing different bills causing trust issues
Edge cases where streaming SDKs don't propagate io_tag
Finance systems unable to represent split-line item on invoices
mitigations: Add end-to-end reconciliation job before experiment start to verify mapping for 200 representative accounts
Expose per-request sample logs to customers on request for first month
SDK patch to ensure io_tag propagation and backwards compatibility
Finance to accept provisional 'floor adjustment' line item during pilot
notes: We expect models with heavy context prep (retrieval + prompt expansion) to increase input tokens; separating IO may lower friction for retrieval-heavy apps
Streaming discount aims to reflect reduced compute per-token when tokens are generated incrementally but requires kernel-level billing hooks
Contract floor is framed as minimum committed spend and can be offset against usage; sales must present a clear ROI
